activity.summary: Waiting for the operator to accept the plan and approve the first billable step

brief.app_summary: demo-app: a small web app with a web front end, an HTTP API and a PostgreSQL database, packaged as a Docker Compose project.

components.name: web
components.role: Serves the front end and forwards /api requests to the api service

components.name: api
components.role: HTTP API that reads and writes items in the database

brief.topology: One VM runs all three containers with Docker Compose. Only the web container is exposed, on port 80; api and db stay internal.
brief.resource_rationale: Three small containers with low expected traffic fit on one small VM. A single VM keeps cost and moving parts low and is easy to tear down.

heavier_alternatives.why_unnecessary: Three containers on one host need no scheduler or node pool.
The data set is small and a trial run does not need managed backups; tier C is offered if wanted.
One VM serves the expected traffic directly.

assumptions: Expected traffic is under 50 requests per minute (not confirmed by the operator)
No public DNS name is needed for this run

tiers.name: Small single VM
tiers.composition: 1 × e2-small VM (2 shared vCPU, 2 GB), 30 GB balanced disk, ephemeral IP
tiers.load_assumption: Up to about 20 requests per minute
tiers.uncertainty: 2 GB of memory may be tight during the first image build

tiers.name: Medium single VM
tiers.composition: 1 × e2-medium VM (2 shared vCPU, 4 GB), 30 GB balanced disk, ephemeral IP
tiers.load_assumption: Up to about 100 requests per minute

tiers.name: VM with managed database
tiers.composition: 1 × e2-small VM plus the smallest shared-core managed PostgreSQL instance
tiers.load_assumption: Up to about 20 requests per minute
tiers.uncertainty: Managed database adds a second billable service and a connection setup step

pending_decision.action: Create one e2-medium VM (tier B) with a 30 GB disk in us-central1-a, allow HTTP on port 80, and start the three containers on it.
pending_decision.why: Tier B is the smallest shape that builds the images comfortably and serves the expected traffic. The tiers and the reasons heavier options are unnecessary are shown in the plan.
pending_decision.cost_or_blast_radius: About 28–36 USD per month while it runs. Only new resources named demo-app-* are created; nothing existing is changed.
pending_decision.reversibility: Reversible: deleting the VM stops compute and disk charges.
pending_decision.rollback: Delete demo-app-vm (its boot disk and ephemeral IP go with it) and the demo-app-allow-http firewall rule.
pending_decision.success_check: The web health endpoint answers on the VM IP and the web → api → db chain returns data.

reply_options.meaning: Accept the plan and create tier B
Accept the plan with the smaller, cheaper VM
Create nothing yet and revise the plan
